A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LitVISTA benchmark and VISTA framework. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support comparison across revisions, relocations, and shortened examples.

before.justification: V1 reports original oracle evaluations of 27 models in Table 2, end-to-end evaluations in Appendix E, and corpus analyses in Figures 5–6.

after.justification: V2 retains the original model evaluations and corpus analyses, including the end-to-end outcomes in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The three-role VISTA framework, single-pass graph reconstruction task, and both evaluation prompts remain unchanged. New serialization explanations address intermediate heads already present in v1's examples; they do not establish a changed prediction procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LitBank-based English literary coverage and oracle and raw-text reconstruction tasks. Shortening the displayed Alice example does not establish reduced training or evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same 27 models, and Appendix E.1 retains the same six end-to-end comparators. All four models illustrated in Appendix E.2 remain represented despite shorter output excerpts.

E3.justification: The 8:1:1 split, oracle versus raw-text conditions, one-shot prompts, and temperature settings remain unchanged. Expanded descriptions of annotation filtering and evaluation clarify existing procedures without establishing revised experimental settings.

E4.justification: The long-range dependency, lexical-role, and end-to-end error analyses remain. Supporting case evidence is reduced: Appendix C shortens the Alice annotation, and Appendix E.2 omits portions of three representative model outputs.

E5.justification: Both report annotation consistency of 0.49 and 0.76 without changing statistical estimation or uncertainty reporting. V2 explains why adjudication has no independent agreement score. Neither reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2, plotted results, and the uniformly zero end-to-end finding are unchanged. Appendix E.2 removes 27 displayed prediction rows: IDs 8–16 from GPT-5-Thinking, DeepSeek-v3.2, and Gemini-3-Pro-Preview-Thinking. Retained entries are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 revises Axiom 5.1 to specify ultimate backbone dependence and adds Axioms 5.1.1–5.1.2 distinguishing ultimate dependence from operational serialization. These qualify the formal treatment of intermediate references; the main equations and remaining axioms are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion explicitly position narrative reconstruction as a diagnostic proxy for generation, with the conclusion excluding direct generation evaluation. They also foreground the existing end-to-end extraction failures. The framework, benchmark, and principal oracle findings remain the core contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds the limitation that participants and character interactions are not explicitly modeled. It also qualifies graph scores as incomplete measures of literary understanding and explains how upstream extraction affects pipeline scores. Existing oracle, domain, scalability, and subjectivity limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 adds the protocol designer's role, annotator pair composition, limited trigger filtering, and dependency-handling details. V1's 1.5-month annotation duration is omitted. The evaluation prompts, temperature information, and dataset access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 removes citations to Bruner (1990), Grimshaw (1990), Ricoeur (1979), Stewart (1986), Tenny (1995), and Graciotti et al. (2025). This prunes supporting literature while retaining the broad research positioning. Bibliographic updates to retained works do not constitute new cited research.

P1.justification: The revision substantially edits the abstract, introductory framing, annotation account, evaluation setup, and conclusion. Section 3.2 is reorganized into background, details, and summary subsections; acknowledgements are added, and appendix explanations and examples are streamlined. This is a broad editorial revision despite stable experiments.

P2.justification: All six numbered figures retain identical image content, and both main tables retain their structure. Figures move with the revised text, Figure 3's caption specifies independent annotation, Appendix A and E prose adopts two columns, and several example displays are shortened.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves interpretability through clearer benchmark scope, fuller annotation documentation, and explicit dependency-serialization conventions. These gains outweigh the reduced appendix detail, but inconsistencies remain: Appendix E.2 still promises 17 initial GPT-5-Thinking anchors while showing eight, and E.1 still mislabels the 0.8135 precision as F1. The improvement is principally in explanation and transparency.
